unit_description: This unit explores how the same area can be arranged in different ways. Students create rectangles with a given area, find different arrangements, find missing side lengths, and decompose rectangles using the distributive property.
unit_goals: Create rectangles with a given area.
Find different arrangements for the same area.
Find a missing side length given area and one side.
Decompose rectangles using the distributive property.

weeks.weekly_focus: Students create rectangles with a given area, explore multiple arrangements, find missing sides, and decompose rectangles with the distributive property.

lessons.lesson_title: Create Rectangles with a Given Area
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by listing factor pairs for a given number.
lessons.concept: A rectangle with a given area can have different lengths and widths. The factor pairs of the area give the possible side lengths.
lessons.practice: Create rectangles with a given area by finding factor pairs.
lessons.objective: Create rectangles with a given area.

questions.prompt: What are the factor pairs for 12?
A rectangle has area 18 square units. What could the length and width be?

learn.title: Create Rectangles with a Given Area
teaching_points: List the factor pairs of the area.
Each factor pair is a possible length and width.
Draw the rectangle for each pair.

example.prompt: Create rectangles with area 20 square units.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Create a rectangle with area 16 square units. What could the length and width be?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Find all possible rectangles with the given area.

bigIdea.title: Create Rectangles with a Given Area
bigIdea.subtitle: Use factor pairs
bigIdea.intro: If you know the area, you can find all the possible rectangles by listing the factor pairs. Each factor pair becomes a length and width.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How are factor pairs related to rectangles with a given area?

ruleCards.description: Each factor pair gives a length and width.
The same area can make different-looking rectangles.

lessons.lesson_title: Find Different Arrangements for the Same Area
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by drawing two different rectangles with the same area.
lessons.concept: Different rectangles can have the same area. Changing the length and width changes the shape, but the total number of square units stays the same.
lessons.practice: Draw and compare different arrangements with the same area.
lessons.objective: Find different arrangements for the same area.

questions.prompt: Draw a 2 by 6 rectangle and a 3 by 4 rectangle. What is the area of each?
Can a 1 by 18 and a 3 by 6 rectangle have the same area?
Name two different rectangles with area 24 square units.

learn.title: Find Different Arrangements for the Same Area
teaching_points: Use factor pairs to find arrangements.
Different side lengths can give the same area.

example.prompt: Find different rectangles with area 18 square units.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Find two different rectangles with area 20 square units.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Draw all possible arrangements for each given area.

flashcards.title: Same Area, Different Shapes
flashcards.instructions: Review same area with different arrangements.

bigIdea.title: Find Different Arrangements for the Same Area
bigIdea.subtitle: Same area, different rectangles
bigIdea.intro: The same area can be arranged in different ways. A long, skinny rectangle can have the same area as a short, wide one.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Can two different rectangles have the same area?

ruleCards.description: Factor pairs of 12 give different rectangles.
Different side lengths can have the same area.

lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by dividing area by one side length.
lessons.concept: If you know the area of a rectangle and one side length, you can find the missing side by dividing. Missing side = area ÷ known side.
lessons.practice: Find the missing side length of rectangles given area and one side.
lessons.objective: Find a missing side length given area and one side.

questions.prompt: Area is 28. One side is 4. What is the other side?
Area is 45. One side is 9. What is the other side?
Area is 36. One side is 6. What is the other side?

learn.title: Find a Missing Side Length
teaching_points: Divide the area by the known side.

example.prompt: A rectangle has area 32 square units and width 4. Find the length.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: A rectangle has area 42 square units and length 7. What is the width?

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Find the missing side length for each rectangle.

bigIdea.title: Find a Missing Side Length
bigIdea.subtitle: Divide area by known side
bigIdea.intro: If you know the area and one side of a rectangle, you can find the other side by dividing. This works because area = length × width.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: Why does area ÷ one side give the other side?

ruleCards.description: You know the area and one side.
Divide the area by the known side.

lessons.lesson_title: Decompose Rectangles Using the Distributive Property
lessons.fact_drill: Warm up by breaking a rectangle into two smaller rectangles and finding each area.
lessons.concept: A large rectangle can be split into two smaller rectangles. The total area is the sum of the two smaller areas. This is the distributive property: 8 × 6 = (8 × 3) + (8 × 3) = 48.
lessons.practice: Decompose rectangles and use the distributive property to find area.
lessons.objective: Decompose rectangles using the distributive property.

questions.prompt: A rectangle 8 by 5 is split into 8 by 2 and 8 by 3. What is the total area?

learn.title: Decompose Rectangles Using the Distributive Property
teaching_points: Split the length or width into two parts.
Find the area of each smaller rectangle.

example.prompt: Find the area of a 7 by 6 rectangle by splitting 6 into 4 + 2.

try_it.title: Try one together
try_it.prompt: Find the area of an 8 by 7 rectangle by splitting 7 into 5 + 2.

practice_block.title: Practice Time
practice_block.instructions: Decompose each rectangle and use the distributive property to find the area.

flashcards.title: Distributive Property and Area
flashcards.instructions: Review decomposing rectangles with the distributive property.

bigIdea.title: Decompose Rectangles Using the Distributive Property
bigIdea.subtitle: Split and add the areas
bigIdea.intro: You can break a rectangle into two smaller rectangles, find each area, and add them. This is the distributive property with area.
bigIdea.bigQuestion: How is decomposing a rectangle like using the distributive property?

ruleCards.description: Split one side into two parts.
Add the areas of the smaller rectangles.
